q: To whom did James write this letter?
a: James wrote this letter to the twelve tribes that were scattered.

q: When experiencing troubles, what attitude does James say his readers should have?
a: James says to consider it all joy when experiencing troubles.

q: What does the testing of our faith produce?
a: The testing of our faith produces endurance.

q: For what should we ask from God if we need it?
a: We should ask God for wisdom if we need it.

q: What is a doubter like?
a: Someone who doubts is like a wave in the sea that is tossed around by the wind.

q: What should someone who asks with doubting expect to receive?
a: Someone who asks with doubting should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.

q: Why should the rich be humble?
a: The rich should be humble because he will pass away just like the flowers.

q: To what can the rich be compared?
a: The rich can be compared to the flower of the grass that dries up, falls off, and perishes.

q: Those who pass the test of faith will receive what?
a: Those who pass the test of faith will receive the crown of life.

q: What causes a person to be tempted by evil?
a: A person’s own evil desires cause him to be tempted by evil.

q: What is the result of full-grown sin?
a: The result of full-grown sin is death.

q: What comes down from the Father of lights?
a: Every good gift and every perfect gift comes down from the Father of lights.

q: By what means did God choose to give us life?
a: God chose to give us life by the word of truth.

q: What does James tell us to do about our hearing, speaking, and emotions?
a: James tells us to be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger.

q: How does James say that we can deceive ourselves?
a: James says that we can deceive ourselves by hearing the word and not doing it.

q: What must be controlled in order for us to be truly religious?
a: The tongue must be controlled in order for us to be truly religious.

q: What is pure and undefiled religion before God?
a: Pure and undefiled religion before God is to visit the fatherless and widows, and to protect ourselves from the world’s corruption.

q: What attitude should believers not have?
a: They should not have an attitude of favoritism.

q: What are believers telling a rich man who enters their meeting?
a: They are telling him to come up front into the best location.

q: What are believers telling a poor man who enters their meeting?
a: They are telling him to stand far away or in a poor location.

q: What have the believers become because of their favoritism?
a: They have become judges of evil thoughts.

q: What does James say about God’s choice of the poor?
a: James says that God chose the poor to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom.

q: What does James say the rich have been doing?
a: James says the rich have been oppressing the brothers and blaspheming God’s name.

q: What is the royal law of the scriptures?
a: The royal law is, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

q: Whoever breaks one point of God’s law is guilty of what?
a: Whoever breaks one point of God’s law is guilty of breaking all the law.

q: What comes to those who have not shown mercy?
a: Judgment without mercy comes to those who have not shown mercy.

q: What does James say about those who claim to have faith, but do not help those in need?
a: James says that those who claim to have faith but do not help those in need have a faith that cannot save them.

q: Does it help a poor person if we tell them to be warmed and filled, but do not give them anything?
a: No, it does not help a poor person if we do not give them anything to warm or feed them.

q: What is faith by itself, if it has no works?
a: Faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead.

q: How does James say we must show our faith?
a: James says we must show our faith by our works.

q: What do demons and those who claim to have faith both believe?
a: Those who claim to have faith and demons both believe there is one God.

q: How did Abraham demonstrate his faith by his works?
a: Abraham demonstrated his faith by his works when he offered up Isaac upon the altar.

q: How was the faith of Abraham perfected?
a: Abraham’s faith was perfected by his works.

q: What scripture was fulfilled with Abraham’s faith and works?
a: The scripture was fulfilled which says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”

q: How did Rahab demonstrate her faith by her works?
a: Rahab demonstrated her faith by her works when she welcomed the messengers and sent them away by another road.

q: What is a body apart from the spirit?
a: A body apart from the spirit is dead.

q: Why does James say that not many should become teachers?
a: Not many should become teachers because they will receive greater judgment.

q: Who stumbles, and in how many ways?
a: We all stumble in many ways.

q: What kind of person is able to control his whole body?
a: A person who does not stumble in his words is also able to control his whole body.

q: What little thing is able to steer a large ship where the pilot wants it to go?
a: A small rudder is able to steer a large ship.

q: What small thing is able to start a large fire in a forest?
a: A small fire is able to start a large fire in a forest.

q: What is the sinful tongue able to do to the whole body?
a: The sinful tongue is able to defile the whole body.

q: What has no one among man been able to tame?
a: No one among man has been able to tame the tongue.

q: What two ways to people treat God and men with their tongues?
a: With a single tongue, they bless God and curse men.

q: What two things can a spring not provide?
a: One spring cannot provide both sweet and bitter water.

q: How does a person demonstrate wisdom and understanding?
a: A person demonstrates wisdom and understanding by his works done in humility.

q: Where kind of wisdom causes a person to be jealous and ambitious, and to lie?
a: Wisdom that is earthly, soulish, and demonic causes a person to be jealous and ambitious, and to lie.

q: What results from jealousy and ambition?
a: Jealousy and ambition causes unsettledness and every wicked deed.

q: What attitudes reflect a wisdom from above?
a: A person that is peace-loving, gentle, warm-hearted, full of mercy and good fruit, without favoritism, and sincere has wisdom from above.

q: What does James say is the source of quarreling and disputing among the believers?
a: The source is the evil desires that war among them.

q: Why do the believers not receive their requests to God?
a: They do not receive because they ask for bad things to be spent on their evil desires.

q: If a person decides to be a friend of the world, what is that person’s relationship with God?
a: A person who decides to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.

q: Who does God resist, and to whom does he give grace?
a: God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.

q: What will the devil do when a believer subjects himself to God and resists the devil?
a: The devil will flee.

q: What will God do for those who draw near to him?
a: God will draw near to those who draw near to him.

q: What does James tell the believers not to do?
a: James tells the believers not to speak against one another.

q: What does James tell the believers to say about what will happen in the future?
a: James tells the believers to say that if the Lord allows, we will live and do this or that.

q: What does James say about those who boast about their plans?
a: James says that those who boast about their plans are doing evil.

q: What is it if someone knows to do good, but does not do it?
a: It is sin if someone knows to do good, but does not do it.

q: What have the rich, about whom James is talking, done in the last days which will testify against them?
a: The rich have hoarded their treasure.

q: How have these rich treated their workers?
a: These rich have not paid their workers.

q: How have these rich treated the righteous man?
a: These rich have condemned and killed the righteous man.

q: What does James say the believer’s attitude should be toward the coming of the Lord?
a: The believers should wait patiently for the coming of the Lord.

q: Why should believers strengthen their hearts as they wait patiently for the coming of the Lord?
a: They should strengthen their hearts because the coming of the Lord is near.

q: What should the suffering and the patience of the Old Testament prophets become for us?
a: The suffering and the patience of the Old Testament prophets should become an example for us.

q: What positive character trait did Job demonstrate?
a: Job demonstrated endurance.

q: What does James say about the reliability of a believer’s “Yes” and “No”?
a: A believer’s “Yes” must mean “Yes” and his “No” must mean “No.”

q: What should those who are sick do?
a: The sick should call for the elders so they can pray over him and anoint him with oil.

q: What two things does James say believers should do with each other in order to be healed?
a: Believers should confess to one another and pray for one another.

q: What happened when Elijah prayed that it would not rain?
a: It did not rain on the land for three years and six months.

q: What happened when Elijah prayed again, this time for rain?
a: When he prayed again, the heaven gave rain and the earth produced fruit.

q: What does someone accomplish who leads a sinner out of the error of his way?
a: The person who leads a sinner out of the error of his way saves a soul from death and covers a multitude of sins.
